siteUrl.title: Site URL
siteUrl.description: Root URL of the WordPress site (e.g. https://example.com) — WordPress is self-hosted, so there is no vendor host and this is required per connection. Do NOT string-concatenate '/wp-json': the REST prefix is filterable (rest_get_url_prefix()) and sites without pretty permalinks are reached as /?rest_route=/wp/v2/posts. Derive the API root from the site's advertised REST URL — the 'Link: <...>; rel="https://api.w.org/"' response header or the equivalent homepage <link> element — and fall back to {siteUrl}/wp-json/ then {siteUrl}/?rest_route=/.

username.title: Username
username.description: WordPress user login that owns the Application Password. Sent as the HTTP Basic username (RFC 7617). The user's capabilities bound what the sync can read: many fields are exposed only for context=edit plus the matching capability, so an under-privileged user silently returns a thinner schema.

applicationPassword.title: Application Password
applicationPassword.description: WordPress Application Password (core since 5.6; wp-admin -> Users -> Edit User), sent as the HTTP Basic password over https://. This ONE credential authenticates BOTH wp/v2 and wc/v3, because wc/v3 routes are ordinary WP REST routes behind capability checks. Requires TLS: wp_is_application_passwords_supported() returns is_ssl() || 'local' === wp_get_environment_type(), and availability is further filterable via 'wp_is_application_passwords_available'.

wooConsumerKey.title: WooCommerce Consumer Key (optional)
wooConsumerKey.description: Optional WooCommerce REST API consumer key (ck_...). Needed only for deployments where an Application Password cannot be used or is not wanted: no TLS (Woo falls back to OAuth 1.0a one-legged), hosts that strip the Authorization header (Woo also accepts ?consumer_key=&consumer_secret=), least-privilege preference (a Woo key carries its own read|write|read_write scope enforced per HTTP method), or sites where Application Passwords are filtered off. WARNING: a Woo key CANNOT read wp/v2 at all — WC_REST_Authentication::is_request_to_rest_api() matches only URIs containing the REST prefix followed by 'wc/' or 'wc-'. A Woo-only connection therefore yields a PARTIAL (WooCommerce-only) object set and must raise an explicit capability warning, never an empty-but-green sync.

wooConsumerSecret.title: WooCommerce Consumer Secret (optional)
wooConsumerSecret.description: Optional WooCommerce REST API consumer secret (cs_...). Supply together with wooConsumerKey; it is unused on its own.

anyOf.title: Application Password (preferred — reaches both wp/v2 and wc/v3)
